nodes.name: Fe/F co-doped Ni2P synthesis
nodes.procedure: The FeNiPBA precursor was immersed in a solution of 5.0 M NH4F. After undergoing low-temperature phosphorization under inert gas, Fe/F–Ni2P@NC was formed.
nodes.source_text: To achieve F doping, the FeNiPBA precursor was immersed in a solution of 5.0 M NH4F. After undergoing low-temperature phosphorization under inert gas, Fe/F–Ni2P@NC was formed

nodes.name: Ce-doped Ni3N hierarchical nanosheets
nodes.procedure: Novel and efficient electrocatalyst comprising N vacancies-enriched, Ce-doped Ni3N hierarchical nanosheets supported on carbon cloth (Ce-Ni3N@CC) was synthesized to optimize UOR kinetics.
nodes.source_text: Fu et al. recently reported a novel and efficient electrocatalyst comprising N vacancies-enriched, Ce-doped Ni3N hierarchical nanosheets supported on carbon cloth (Ce-Ni3N@CC)

nodes.name: Rh nanosheets from trigonal RhO2
nodes.procedure: Porous rhodium nanosheets (Rh-NSs) with tunable lattice strain were successfully synthesized by direct annealing of metastable trigonal rhodium oxide (Tri-RhO2) nanosheets in a hydrogen atmosphere.
nodes.source_text: porous rhodium nanosheets (Rh-NSs) with tunable lattice strain were successfully synthesized by direct annealing of metastable trigonal rhodium oxide (Tri-RhO2) nanosheets in a hydrogen atmosphere

nodes.name: Pt on oxygen vacancy-rich CeO2
nodes.procedure: CeO2 nanorods with rich oxygen vacancies (vo) and a rough surface were used as the Pt support to engineer the metal-oxide interface.
nodes.source_text: Wang et al. used the CeO2 nanorods with rich oxygen vacancies (vo) and a rough surface as the Pt support

nodes.characterization_summary: Fe/F co-doping results in intermediate d-band center facilitating balanced adsorption/desorption processes and improves HzOR dehydrogenation thermodynamics.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Fe, F co-doping resulted in an intermediate d-band center, facilitating balanced adsorption and desorption processes and thereby improving bifunctional catalytic performance. Furthermore, DFT calculations indicated that Fe/F doping enhances the thermodynamic behavior of the dehydrogenation process in the HzOR...

nodes.characterization_summary: Ce incorporation into Ni3N reduces N vacancy formation energy, resulting in high density of N vacancies that optimize local charge distribution around Ni sites and balance CO2 adsorption energy.
nodes.evidence_snippet: DFT calculations revealed that the incorporation of Ce into Ni3N reduces the formation energy of N vacancies (Fig. 4a), resulting in a high density of N vacancies in Ce-Ni3N@CC. Furthermore, the N vacancies, in combination with Ce doping, optimize the local charge distribution around the Ni sites...

nodes.characterization_summary: Compressive strain in Rh-NSs reduces Gibbs free energy of the potential-determining step in HzOR.
nodes.evidence_snippet: DFT calculations indicated that Rh-NSs with tunable compressive strain could reduce the Gibbs free energy...

nodes.characterization_summary: V doping generates oxygen vacancies and exposed edge sites in Ni(OH)2, shifting UOR rate-determining step from *COOH deprotonation to N–H bond cleavage, lowering thermodynamic barrier by 1.13 eV vs pristine γ-NiOOH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: V doping not only generates more exposed edge active sites but also introduces oxygen vacancies, shifting the rate-determining step of the UOR from *COOH deprotonation to the N–H bond cleavage process. This modification lowers the thermodynamic barrier by approximately 1.13 eV compared to pristine γ-NiOOH (Fig. 4b)...

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ FTIR shows n-valeraldehyde characteristic peaks at 1751, 2712, 2970 cm⁻¹ on Au0.3SACs-NiMn2O4 with increasing intensity over time; n-valeric acid peak at 1712 cm⁻¹ forms then decreases indicating reaction progression.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the characteristic peaks of n-valeraldehyde are observed at 1751, 2712, and 2970 cm⁻¹... For Au0.3SACs-NiMn2O4, the intensity of n-valeraldehyde peaks gradually increases with prolonged reaction time... The appearance of a peak at 1712 cm⁻¹ indicates... n-valeric acid formation.

nodes.characterization_summary: CV confirms significantly improved water dissociation ability at single-atom Ru sites in Ru1–NiO enabling HMF oxidation at 1.283 V for 10 mA cm⁻² in 1.0 M PBS with 50 mM HMF.
nodes.evidence_snippet: For the oxidation reaction of 5-hydroxymethyl furfural (HMF) in a 1.0 M phosphate buffer solution (PBS), Ru1–NiO shows a low potential of 1.283 V at 10 mA cm⁻²... Through a combination of cyclic voltammetry (CV)... the authors revealed that the remarkable activity of Ru1–NiO ascribed to the significantly improved water dissociation ability occurring at the single-atom Ru sites.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiCo@C/MXene/CF shows CA_bubble = 153° enabling rapid release of small gas bubbles <60-80 μm during HER.
nodes.evidence_snippet: this electrode possesses a remarkably high contact angle for gas bubbles (CA_bubble = 153°), which effectively facilitates the rapid release of small gas bubbles (<60-80 μm) during the electrolysis process
